items.title: 1.8 Interpreting the Relation Between a One-to-One Function and Its Inverse through Graph (Roman Urdu)

blocks.text: Is unit mein hum ne exponential aur logarithmic functions ko ek doosre ka inverse kaha. Ab sawal yeh hai ke kisi function ka inverse kab banta hai, aur graph par function aur us ke inverse mein kya rishta hota hai? Yeh topic isi ka jawab hai, aur agla subtopic 1.8.1 isay graph bana kar dikhata hai.

Kitab kehti hai: kisi function ka inverse sirf tab hota hai jab woh bijective ho, yani one-to-one bhi ho aur onto bhi. Lekin agar function ka co-domain (woh set jis mein outputs jaane chahiye) us ke range (woh set jo outputs asal mein aate hain) ke barabar le liya jaye, to co-domain ki har value function pehle hi hasil kar leta hai. Is liye function khud ba khud onto ban jata hai, aur inverse ke liye sirf one-to-one wali shart reh jati hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Dono shartein kyun? Inverse \(f^{-1}\) ko har output wapas sirf ek input tak le jana hai. Agar \(f\) one-to-one na ho to koi output do inputs se aata hai, aur \(f^{-1}\) faisla nahi kar sakta ke kis par wapas jaye. Misaal: \(f(x) = x^{2}\) (\(\mathbb{R}\) par) mein \(f(2) = f(-2) = 4\); ab 4 ka inverse 2 hai ya \(-2\)? Pata nahi. Agar \(f\) onto na ho to co-domain ki kuch values ka koi input hi nahi, to un ka inverse kahan jaye?
Rozmarra ki misaal: class mein har student ka roll number alag hai (one-to-one), is liye roll number se student wapas pehchana ja sakta hai. Agar do students ka roll number same ho to roll number se student dhoondna mumkin nahi.
Kitab ki baat: co-domain ko range ke barabar rakh lein to onto hona khud mil jata hai. Amal mein hum sirf one-to-one check karte hain, maslan horizontal line test se.

Kitab aage kehti hai: function aur us ke inverse ke graph line \(y = x\) ke gird ek geometric symmetry (aaine jaisi barabari) se jure hote hain. Yahi line kyun? Kyun ke function par har point \((x, y)\) ek input-output jori hai, aur inverse mein input aur output ke kirdar badal jate hain. Line \(y = x\) bilkul un points ka set hai jahan input aur output barabar hain, is liye yahi is adla badli ka qudrati aaina (axis of reflection) hai.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Yeh misaal hamari taraf se hai: \(f(x) = 2x + 3\). Yeh one-to-one hai (seedhi line, har horizontal line isay ek hi jagah kaat-ti hai). Is ka inverse nikalne ke liye \(y = 2x + 3\) mein \(x\) aur \(y\) badal kar \(y\) nikaalein: \(x = 2y + 3 \Rightarrow y = \frac{x - 3}{2}\). To \(f^{-1}(x) = \frac{x - 3}{2}\).
Ab \(f(1) = 5\), yani \((1, 5)\) \(f\) ke graph par hai. Aur \(f^{-1}(5) = \frac{5 - 3}{2} = 1\), yani \((5, 1)\) \(f^{-1}\) ke graph par hai. Coordinates ne jagah badal li.
Kya yeh do points \(y = x\) mein aaina hain? Un ka midpoint \((3, 3)\) hai, jo \(y = x\) par hai. Aur un ko jorne wali line ka slope \(\frac{1 - 5}{5 - 1} = -1\) hai, jo \(y = x\) (slope 1) par perpendicular (amood) hai. Haan, bilkul aaina.
Khud sochiye: agar \((4, 9)\) kisi one-to-one function par hai to us ke inverse par kaun sa point hoga? (Jawab: \((9, 4)\).)

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. Inverse tab banta hai jab \(f\) one-to-one aur onto ho; co-domain = range rakhein to sirf one-to-one kaafi hai.
2. \(f\) par \((p, q)\) \(\Leftrightarrow\) \(f^{-1}\) par \((q, p)\).
3. \(f\) aur \(f^{-1}\) ke graphs line \(y = x\) mein ek doosre ka aaina hain.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. \(f^{-1}(x)\) ko \(\frac{1}{f(x)}\) samajhna. Yahan \(-1\) ka matlab inverse function hai, reciprocal (ulta kasar) nahi.
2. \(x\)-axis ya \(y\)-axis mein reflection le lena; inverse ke liye aaina hamesha line \(y = x\) hai.
3. Aise function ka inverse banane ki koshish jo one-to-one nahi, jaise \(\mathbb{R}\) par \(x^{2}\).
